nodes.name: Sanctum league (The Forbidden Sanctum)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.20.0 (9 Dec 2022 - 4 Apr 2023; shipped as 'Path of Exile: The Forbidden Sanctum'): a roguelite run through an ancient Templar enclave beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, controlled by a malevolent entity (Lycia is its fourth-floor boss).

nodes.name: The Forbidden Sanctum
nodes.summary: Ancient Templar enclave/ossuary-library beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, four floors deep, abandoned for a long time and now controlled by Lycia, who lures treasure hunters in through portals; floors shift from tidy library to Scourge-infested crypt.

sources.locator: '==Lore==': 'ancient Templar enclave hidden beneath the Fellshrine Ruins'
[4:05]-[4:30] four floors, library to crypt; [10:35]-[11:30] ossuary and pact

nodes.name: Fellshrine Ruins
nodes.summary: Ruined former Freesia Cathedral area of Wraeclast, above the Forbidden Sanctum; Eramir calls the Fellshrine a shadow of what was once good in Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Divinia
nodes.summary: Templar archivist and relic enthusiast met at the Oriath Docks in Act 10 (quest 'Aiding an Archivist'); she sends the Exile for the Mortinomicon Exitio Immortalis and later sells relics inside the Sanctum. She knows far more about Lycia and the Scourge than she lets on; her true motives are left ambiguous.

sources.locator: 'Talk to Divinia in Oriath Docks'; Mortinomicon dialogue
[1:24]-[1:50], [12:24]-[13:20], [36:38]-[37:15] (video places her meeting in Act 2 camp; wiki says Oriath Docks Act 10)

nodes.name: Lycia, Herald of the Scourge
nodes.summary: Former Templar scholar and keeper of forbidden knowledge who, disillusioned by the truth of Innocence's origins and the Templars' unmarked ossuary bones, made a pact with the Scourge demon Beidat for immortality; imprisoned in the Sanctum she is its fourth-floor boss and league antagonist.

chronology.relative: lived sometime after the Eternal Empire's founding; exact date unknown (video guesses c. 1000-1300 IC)

sources.locator: page summary: former Templar, necromancy and lithomancy, immortality in pact with Beidat

nodes.name: Beidat
nodes.summary: Leader of the 'pale demons', one of the three Scourge factions; unlike the headless-drone demon and flesh factions he can speak and bargain with humans, and gave Lycia immortality.

nodes.name: Maxarius
nodes.summary: Per the Sanctum relic texts (as recounted in the wiki and video), Maxarius, the first High Templar, was in truth Innocence himself - a charlatan who stole the Descry symbol from fire-terrified newcomers, used their fear, and vilified his brother Sin to ascend.

chronology.relative: ancient, when the Azmeri still lived in the Azmerian mountains

sources.locator: [28:00]-[30:30] relics reveal Maxarius = Innocence; quote 'a charlatan, a liar and a power seeker'
===Templar history (line ~188): "The very first High Templar, Maxarius, was not Innocence's chosen, as was told, but Innocence himself."
Lore: "He posed himself as Maxarius, the first High Templar, and vilified his own brother as the Original Evil."

nodes.name: Innocence's true ascension (Sanctum relic account)
nodes.summary: Lore revealed through Sanctum unique relics: Sin and Innocence were brothers among the Azmeri; Innocence founded a religion on fear of the 'cleansing fire' and the newcomers' symbol, branded Sin the embodiment of sin, and both ascended (Sin ashen, Innocence golden), until the Azmeri drove Innocence's followers off the mountains. Contradicts the Templar 'mother of two' propaganda.

sources.locator: [24:37]-[32:00] Lycia's relic text account; [43:03]-[44:30] mother of two as fabrication

nodes.name: Lycia's pact with Beidat
nodes.summary: Lycia, shocked by the unnamed discarded bones of the Templar ossuary and the true origin of Innocence, called Beidat and traded her freedom for immortality inside the Sanctum, giving the Scourge a foothold in Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Templar Relics (Sanctum)
nodes.summary: Relics placed on the Sanctum altar to strengthen the Exile across runs; unique relics carry Lycia's written account of Innocence. Aureus is the Templars' coin.

nodes.name: Crucible league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.21.0 (7 Apr - 15 Aug 2023, 'Path of Exile: Crucible'): Crucible Forges grant equipment a passive tree, and Primeval Remnants open portals to the Forge of the Titans.

nodes.name: Forge of the Titans
nodes.summary: Primeval forge reached through Primeval Remnants during Crucible league, where equipment trees are combined; the stone body and voice of the Molten One, the last known Titan, can be met there.

sources.locator: '==League Mechanic==' Primeval Remnant / Forge of the Titans
Molten One entry: 'During Crucible league, his stone body and voice can be encountered in the Forge of the Titans'

nodes.name: The Molten One
nodes.summary: Last surviving Titan from a prehistoric era, worshipped indirectly as the volcano home of the Redblade warband; writes environmental lore found in the Forge of the Titans.

nodes.name: Primeval Remnant
nodes.summary: Currency-like item that opens a portal to the Forge of the Titans; its text recounts the near-extinction of the Titans after the rising darkness (Lightless) of the Winter of the World.

nodes.name: Ancestor league (Trial of the Ancestors)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.22.0 (18 Aug - 5 Dec 2023): Exiles use Silver Coins to enter the Karui afterlife and field a team of Karui warriors in the Trial of the Ancestors tournament against fallen chieftains, under Hinekora.

nodes.name: Trial of the Ancestors
nodes.summary: Tournament in the Halls of the Dead where the Exile's team of Karui warriors fights teams led by the ten Karui chieftains, destroying totems; winning a full tournament earns rewards from Hinekora (omens, Hinekora's Lock, unique items).

sources.locator: 'rules over the Halls of the Dead and oversees the Trial of the Ancestors'

nodes.name: The Halls of the Dead
nodes.summary: Karui afterlife created by Hinekora before the Slumbering of the Gods as a place for Karui souls; where fallen chieftains reside and the Trial of the Ancestors is held.

nodes.name: Affliction league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.23.0 (8 Dec 2023 - 26 Mar 2024): the player cleanses the Affliction of the Viridian Wildwood with sacred wisps, trains with the Azmeri and unlocks Wildwood ascendancy classes; the King in the Mists is the antagonist.

nodes.name: The King in the Mists
nodes.summary: Major antagonist of Affliction league, a shadowy Nameless force within the Viridian Wildwood against whom the Maji wage a long war; later added to Ritual in 3.25.

sources.locator: unique items 'the King in the Mists'
'The King in the Mists encounter added to Ritual'

nodes.name: The Viridian Wildwood
nodes.summary: Haven created by the Draiocht as refuge from the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons; haunted by shadowy creatures such as the King in the Mists; home of the Maji.

nodes.name: Wisps (humours)
nodes.summary: Wildwood humours materialised as Primal, Vivid, Wild and Sacred wisps; freed wisps escape into the overworld empowering monsters; Sacred humours are harvested by the King in the Mists' ritual altars.

nodes.name: The Maji
nodes.summary: Azmeri vanguard sent into the Wildwood to wait while it is purged of evil, waging war on the King in the Mists.

nodes.name: Wildwood ascendancy classes
nodes.summary: Affliction's temporary ascendancies (Wildwood Primalist with charms, Warden of the Maji with tinctures, Warlock of the Mists with corpse items) earned through the Azmeri questlines; removed at league end.

nodes.name: Necropolis league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.24.0 (29 Mar - 23 Jul 2024): Undertaker Arimor lends the Exile his Lantern to haunt monsters, collect their corpses and bury them in the Necropolis for grave crafting; Embers of the Allflame transform monsters.

nodes.name: Undertaker Arimor
nodes.summary: Undertaker who gathers the haunted dead of Wraeclast, gives the Exile the Lantern of Arimor and runs the Necropolis; invokes a god named Thruldana during his chants.

sources.locator: ===Thruldana=== "A god whose name is invoked by Undertaker Arimor during one of his chants."

nodes.name: The Lantern of Arimor
nodes.summary: Heirloom lantern revealing and rearranging the haunting modifiers of monsters before a zone is entered.

nodes.name: The Necropolis
nodes.summary: Graveyard where haunted corpses are buried and exorcised to add crafting modifiers to the Tome of Arimor.

sources.locator: Perform the Exorcism in The Necropolis

nodes.name: The Allflame
nodes.summary: Mysterious flame whose Embers (Necropolis) transform monsters via the Lantern; its light returns in Allflame league as a growing, hungry power that Vesper says differs from the light of the pit below the sea.

nodes.name: House Perandus (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Perandus Pact'.

nodes.name: Tyndarus Phrecius
nodes.summary: Eternal Empire emperor who in 870 IC sent Phrecian legions to Trarthus to suppress the warlords' rebellion and capitulated after two years.

nodes.name: Settlers of Kalguur league
nodes.summary: PoE1 expansion/league 3.25.0 (26 Jul 2024; league ended 9 Jun 2025 22:00 UTC / 10 Jun 2025 00:00 GMT+2 per GGG after multiple extensions for PoE2 Early Access, over 45 weeks): the Exile helps Kalguuran settlers build Kingsmarch, a harbour meant to facilitate trade between the settlers, the Karui archipelago and Kalguur. Town-building ended in 3.26.0; Kingsmarch services joined the core game.

sources.locator: GGG forum "What Will Happen When The Settlers League Ends": "The league will end on Jun 10, 2025 12:00 AM (GMT+2)"; "Kingsmarch will be going core in 3.26"

nodes.name: Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: Kalguuran-chartered port and hub town on the Karui coast, reached via Johan in the Karui Shores (Epilogue). Run by the King's Hand under a Charter, it hosts Dannig, Tujen, Rog, Isla, Faustus, Raulf and Sonja. In PoE2 it is the Act 4 town and later lies in ruins in the endgame.

sources.locator: intro + '==NPCs=='; Trivia 'Act 4 town in Path of Exile 2'

nodes.name: Kalguur
nodes.summary: Homeland of the Kalguurans on the continent Middengard, south-east of Wraeclast; ruled by a mysterious King Cadigan who gives charters to successful outposts.

nodes.name: Middengard
nodes.summary: Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.

nodes.name: Kalguurans
nodes.summary: People of Kalguur: rune-smiths who use runes of starlight, have no gods, lack inherent affinity for virtue gems, and live under King Cadigan; settlers in Wraeclast built Kingsmarch.

nodes.name: King Cadigan
nodes.summary: Mysterious tyrant-king of Kalguur whose name all kings share (possibly one person extending life by artifice); spies on subjects, instituted shipment taxes, has his eye on Wraeclast, and in PoE2 ordered Vaal artifacts brought home.

sources.locator: Negative outcomes: 'The King decided to institute a one-time tax'

nodes.name: King Cadigan the Third
nodes.summary: Ordered the first Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast carrying the Triskelion Flame; banned collection of virtue gems after the Azmeri's fearful reaction.

nodes.name: King Cadigan the First
nodes.summary: Kalguuran king under whom the Triskelion Flame was a symbol of authority; the Flame had earlier been taken by a self-proclaimed descendant of Aldur who had challengers killed.

nodes.name: Aldur
nodes.summary: First Runefather and first king of Kalguur; by legend crafted the first runes.

nodes.name: The Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: Kalguuran relic forged by the Runefathers in honour of Aldur; purifies corrupted food and projects a starlight barrier. Stolen by Olroth, who used it to keep himself alive; destroyed in the encounter with Dannig and the Exile.

nodes.name: First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Centuries-old expedition ordered by Cadigan III including Knights of the Sun, Black Scythe, Druids of the Broken Circle, Priests of the Chalice and Remembrancers; it taught the Ezomytes runesmithing and ended in tragedy.

nodes.name: Olroth
nodes.summary: Leader of the Knights of the Sun (Origin of the Fall / the Gallant / the Grim); stole the Triskelion Flame, doomed the expedition and villages, and was found by Dannig and the Exile sustained by it. Motive unknown.

nodes.name: Uhtred
nodes.summary: Kalguuran expedition member who declared virtue gems unclean and succumbed to corruption-driven madness before discovering a dark mirror.

nodes.name: Vorana
nodes.summary: Leader of the Black Scythe mercenaries; used virtue gems against the nightbreeds and the Empty-Eyed Fiend, casting aside her primary virtue.

nodes.name: Medved
nodes.summary: Leader of the Druids of the Broken Circle of Kalguur, rumoured to see the future by peering into the past; experiments with virtue gems.

nodes.name: Knights of the Sun
nodes.summary: Warriors and military enforcers under direct orders of the King, led by Olroth.

nodes.name: The Black Scythe
nodes.summary: Mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana.

nodes.name: Druids of the Broken Circle
nodes.summary: Nature-mystics led by Medved; PoE2 names Gronel Starseer, Smalon Thickett, Avon Bruhn.

nodes.name: Remembrancers
nodes.summary: Documentarians of Kalguuran explorations.

nodes.name: Priests of the Chalice
nodes.summary: Religious order that read the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes.

nodes.name: Johan, the King's Hand
nodes.summary: Kalguuran official sent to execute Kingsmarch's Charter as the King's Hand and Treasurer; admits loyalty to both the King and the Charter's law; tolerates 'less than upstanding' residents so long as he sees no sedition. He bears a scar given by Gwennen.

nodes.name: Raulf, the Recruiter
nodes.summary: Meridian Free Traders agent who recruits labourers and specialists for Kingsmarch; refuses to be anyone's spy.

nodes.name: Sonja, the Farmer
nodes.summary: Kingsmarch farmer puzzled by the thriving plants on supposedly barren soil.

nodes.name: Dannig, Warrior Skald
nodes.summary: Kalguuran blacksmith and Warrior Skald whose goal is to recover the Triskelion Flame; runesmith, game-night friend of Rog, Tujen and Gwennen; in PoE2 manages Verisium/Runeforging in Kingsmarch.

nodes.name: Tujen, the Haggler / Harbourmaster
nodes.summary: Kalguuran haggler turned Kingsmarch harbourmaster who crews ships; former rebel who lost friends (Tolis, Oskar, Naja, Thea, Sven) and vows revenge; in PoE2 asks the Exile to clear the fog at Kedge Bay.

nodes.name: Rog, the Disenchanter
nodes.summary: Kalguuran dealer who runs the Kingsmarch disenchanting apothecary and dreams of his own shop; manages the group's tabletop game; former rebel.

nodes.name: Gwennen, the Gambler
nodes.summary: Kalguuran gambler and former rebel who avoids Kingsmarch because Johan, scarred by her, could recognise her and expose surviving rebels.

nodes.name: Isla, the Engineer
nodes.summary: Engineer building Kingsmarch's map devices and the Recombinator; her letter ('I'm so happy you're alive!') hints at a past connection with the Exile and mentions Kalguuran runes' strange effect on portals.

nodes.name: Faustus, the Financier
nodes.summary: Former Heist captain turned Kingsmarch financier running the Currency Exchange, respec and Black Market; writes of waiting and watching the King; reported dead in PoE2 ('rest his soul').

nodes.name: Meridian Free Traders
nodes.summary: Trade guild that sent Raulf to assist executing the Kingsmarch charter; in PoE2 it controls boat charters (Makoru captains the Aurora May under it).

nodes.name: Failed Kalguuran rebellion
nodes.summary: Rebellion against the King, referenced by Gwennen and implicated by letters involving Tujen, Rog and Dannig; survivors escaped to Wraeclast while Johan remembers Gwennen's face.

nodes.name: Founding of Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: When a Kalguuran outpost in Wraeclast reached a certain size, the King gifted it an official Charter and the name Kingsmarch and sent Johan as King's Hand; the Exile joins and invests Gold in the town's treasury and services (PoE1 3.25-3.26).

nodes.name: The Kingsmarch Charter
nodes.summary: Royal charter under which Kingsmarch operates; Johan enforces it to the letter, including punishments such as the Royal Order of Criminal Hanging subject to a statute of limitations.

nodes.name: Kingsmarch shipping and trade routes
nodes.summary: Trade shipping from Kingsmarch to Kalguuran ports (Riben Fell, Pondium, Kalguur) and Karui ports (Ngakanu, Te Onui, Moti Aro); risks include pirates, corrupt officials, a royal tax and 'mysterious green light' losses. Pirate Admiral Valerius can commandeer ships.

nodes.name: Kingsmarch workers and town management
nodes.summary: Recruited workers (miners, smelters, farmers, disenchanters, shippers, Atlas runners) are hired through Raulf for Gold; the town runs on real-time resources: ores, bars, crops and thaumaturgic dust.

nodes.name: Kalguuran Map Device
nodes.summary: Isla's portal-based device by which Atlas Runners map and loot the Atlas while the Exile is away; Sasan the Bandit Lord can hold them hostage.

nodes.name: Recombinator
nodes.summary: Isla's prototype that breaks down two matching items and reintegrates them into one new piece.

nodes.name: Kalguuran runesmithing
nodes.summary: Kalguuran art of engraving starlight runes (Verisium from meteorites) into weapons and armour; Ezomytes learned it from the first expedition; revived as Runesmithing in Settlers and Runeforging in PoE2 Act 4.

nodes.name: Riben Fell
nodes.summary: Kalguuran port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

nodes.name: Admiral Valerius
nodes.summary: Pirate boss fought in Sailor's Folly when a shipment is commandeered; can drop Admiral's Arrogance.

nodes.name: The Black Knight
nodes.summary: Boss guarding Verisium Outcrops in the Starfall Crater (reached via map ore deposits); drops Svalinn.

nodes.name: Sasan, the Bandit Lord
nodes.summary: Bandit Lord who takes Atlas Runners hostage while they map; defeat him or pay 50,000 Gold; drops The Living Blade and The Bandit Lord's Band.

nodes.name: Letter (Kingsmarch environmental lore)
nodes.summary: Rotating letters in the Kingsmarch tavern by Johan, Raulf, Sonja, Dannig, Rog, Tujen, Gwennen, Faustus and Isla revealing their secret rebel ties, loves and loyalties.

nodes.name: Necro Settlers event

sources.locator: intro: 'Necro Settlers event was held from November 2024 to February 2025'

nodes.name: The Search (PoE2 Act 4)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Act 4 main quest: the Exile, Doryani, Alva and the Hooded One reach Kingsmarch, hire a boat (Makoru of the Aurora May, under the Meridian Free Traders) and seek the three pieces of the Precursor weapon, ending with Tavakai.

nodes.name: Farrow
nodes.summary: Ezomyte Runeseeker in PoE2 Kingsmarch investigating the origins of runes; hands out the Runeseeker quest.

nodes.name: Ange
nodes.summary: Marketeer in PoE2 Kingsmarch who learned from Rog and Faustus ('rest his soul'); gives Hostile Takeover.

nodes.name: Makoru
nodes.summary: Captain of the Aurora May who ferries the Exile around the Karui islands under the Meridian Free Traders.

nodes.name: The Runeseeker (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Act 4 quest from Farrow: collect Torn Map Pieces for Dannig, unlocking Plunder's Point and Runeforging.

nodes.name: The Grand Expedition (PoE2 endgame)
nodes.summary: Endgame quest in which Farrow worries about Kingsmarch after the chaos and the Exile returns to the Ruins of Kingsmarch to find Dannig, Gwennen, Tujen and Rog and the logbooks of Vorana, Uhtred and Olroth, recovering the Shattered Triskelion.

nodes.name: Dark Mists (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Act 4 quest from Tujen: clear the fog at Kedge Bay (Captain Hartlin), bring Verisium to Dannig and return to Tujen.

nodes.name: Hostile Takeover (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Ange's Act 4 quest to clear the Shoreline Hideout.

nodes.name: Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas
nodes.summary: PoE1 expansion 3.26.0 (13 Jun 2025) containing Mercenaries league and the Originator endgame storyline (Zana the Originator, Eagon Caeserius, Threads of the Originator); Settlers' Kingsmarch services were added to the core game.

nodes.name: Mercenaries league (Mercenaries of Trarthus)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.26.0 (13 Jun - 27 Oct 2025): lawless Trarthan veterans can be fought and hired; noble mercenaries descend from the four death-trade Great Houses.

nodes.name: Trarthus
nodes.summary: Region southwest of Wraeclast and west of the Karui archipelago; capital Korathin; a brutal slave-and-killer culture ruled by four Great Houses, once the Eternal Empire's dumping ground for exiles.

nodes.name: Trarthans
nodes.summary: People of Trarthus descended from Eternal Empire exiles and slaves, led by four Great Houses.

nodes.name: House Keita
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Slave armies, flesh pits; failed to become a god; founded Korathin 872 IC.

nodes.name: Ixan Keita
nodes.summary: Founder of House Keita, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

nodes.name: House Cyaxan
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Drug trade, criminal syndicate and mass virtue gem implantation.

nodes.name: Kylian Cyaxan
nodes.summary: Founder of House Cyaxan, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

nodes.name: House Bardiya
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Financiers; Merchant Council with greatest control today.

nodes.name: Quilon Bardiya
nodes.summary: Founder of House Bardiya, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

nodes.name: House Azadi
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Contract-assassin monopoly.

nodes.name: Ratha Azadi
nodes.summary: Founder of House Azadi, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

nodes.name: Trarthan Rebellion against Phrecius (870 IC)
nodes.summary: Warlords of Trarthus were executed after Phrecian legions occupied it; four first-generation Trarthans led a war; Karui blockades and Ezomyte sabotage doomed reinforcements; Tyndarus capitulated after two years.

nodes.name: Merchant Wars and War of the Great Families
nodes.summary: Feud between House Keita and House Bardiya that escalated into civil war and ended in a ceasefire and the Merchant Council.

nodes.name: Korathin
nodes.summary: Capital of Trarthus, declared by Ixan Keita in 872 IC and built by his slaves.

nodes.name: Trarthan mercenaries
nodes.summary: Lawless Trarthan veterans met in Mercenaries league; hirable allies with unique gear and skills; noble ones come from the four Great Houses.

nodes.name: Zana, the Originator
nodes.summary: Zana Caeserius, the Originator, is trapped in the Atlas weaving memories to destroy it; tells Eagon 'I am not your sister' (ambiguous whether another Zana).

nodes.name: Eagon Caeserius
nodes.summary: Caeserius family member who recruits the Exile to follow Memory Threads to the Originator.

nodes.name: Threads of the Originator
nodes.summary: Epilogue quest starting the Secrets of the Atlas storyline; the Exile follows Memory Threads with Eagon to find the Originator.

nodes.name: Legacy of Phrecia event
nodes.summary: Event (run after the Necro Settlers event until 23 April 2025, with a second run later adding random modifiers) that replaces the 19 ascendancy classes with alternate 'whacky ideas' classes and replaces the Atlas passive tree with an idol system.

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.27.0 (31 Oct 2025 - 2 Mar 2026): the Exile works with Ailith to repel Hiveborn invading via stabilised Breach connections and grows the Genesis Tree; Breach joined the core game in 3.28.0.

nodes.name: Ailith, First of the Keepers
nodes.summary: Leader of the Keepers; tends the Genesis Tree at the Monastery, receives dream warnings, and guides the Exile to graft Breach flesh onto themselves.

nodes.name: The Genesis Tree
nodes.summary: Living tree at the Monastery of the Keepers that consumes Hiveborn remains and hiveblood to birth wombgifts.

nodes.name: Monastery of the Keepers
nodes.summary: Keepers' sanctuary housing Ailith and the Genesis Tree.

nodes.name: Hiveborn
nodes.summary: Mutated Breach monsters spilling into Wraeclast through a stabilised interdimensional link.

nodes.name: Vruun, Marshal of Xesht
nodes.summary: Breach marshal found in stabilised Unstable Breaches; Ailith's PoE1 Keepers quest asks the Exile to bring 'The Head of Vruun' and praises it as preparation for a second graft meld.

nodes.name: It That Was Tul
nodes.summary: Former Breachlord boss in the Hive Colony.

nodes.name: It That Was Esh
nodes.summary: Former Breachlord boss in the Hive Colony (paired with Tul).

nodes.name: Mirage league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.28.0 (6 Mar 2026; scheduled to end 20 Jul 2026): with Sekhema Varashta the Exile frees djinn tortured by the Afarud via mirages and the astral realm; endgame necromancer Saresh.

nodes.name: Varashta, the Winter Sekhema
nodes.summary: Former Maraketh Sekhema who projects herself near mirages and grants wishes; opposes Zarokh, the Grand Djinn of Time.

nodes.name: Zarokh, Grand Djinn of Time
nodes.summary: Djinn who siphons other djinn to project power; his mirage is bound by an Astral Chain.

nodes.name: The Afarud
nodes.summary: Rogue Faridun sect that torments djinn; led by figures such as Ridan, Afarud Commander.

nodes.name: Ridan, Afarud Commander
nodes.summary: Afarud boss in mirages; drops The Black Barya.

nodes.name: Saresh, of the Weeping Black
nodes.summary: Historical Faridun necromancer and Order of the Djinn member slain by Garukhan; endgame boss in The Black Barya.

nodes.name: Faridun
nodes.summary: Maraketh outcasts left to die in the Vastiri, resentful and necromancy-dabbling; antagonists in PoE2 Act 2.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamities; Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.

nodes.name: Allflame league (Curse of the Allflame)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.29.0 (24 Jul 2026; announced end 9 Nov 2026): aboard Valerie's ship the Sovereign, Exiles chart the Fathomless Depths with Allflame lanterns and craft with Vesper.

nodes.name: Valerie, the Corsair
nodes.summary: Pondium-born corsair captain who borrowed the Sovereign from its masked, Templar-linked builders and freed Vesper's soul; recruits Exiles as first mates.

sources.locator: Dialogue: The Forge, Pondium, The Sovereign

nodes.name: Vesper
nodes.summary: Valerie's childhood friend whose body lies aboard the Sovereign while his soul is bound to the ship; runs Allflame crafting.

nodes.name: The Sovereign
nodes.summary: Ship built in an underground pit-laboratory by masked men working for the Templars using a tortured prisoner, Vesper, as its heart; fuelled by Dead Man's Sulphur and the Allflame.

nodes.name: The Fathomless Depths
nodes.summary: Underwater endgame area explored via a Bathysphere and Allflame lanterns; a pit of deathly light lies below.

nodes.name: Brinerot
nodes.summary: Pirate/whaler warband of the sea whose corsairs ambush chart-seekers; their Shamanessa Velka traffics with the dead.

nodes.name: Velka, the Tide Witch
nodes.summary: Brinerot Shamanessa hunting the Allflame; boss in Kishara's Rest.

nodes.name: Pondium (Valerie's home port)
nodes.summary: Lawless port where Valerie and Vesper grew up; Valerie says it holds more fairness than Oriath.

nodes.name: Starfall Crater
nodes.summary: Area reached through an entrance that can randomly appear in ore-deposit maps; holds The Black Knight, who guards several Verisium Outcrops (Kingsmarch wiki, Bosses section).

sources.locator: ==Bosses== ===The Black Knight===: "Map areas containing ore deposits can randomly contain an entrance to the Starfall Crater, which holds the Black Knight inside guarding several Verisium Outcrops."

nodes.name: Verisium
nodes.summary: Metal ore found only in fallen meteorites and not native to Wraeclast; Kalguuran runes were typically crafted from it, and in PoE2 Act 4 Dannig forges Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots.

sources.locator: ===Runes===: "Runes were typically crafted using Verisium, a type of metal ore found only from fallen meteorites, and not native to Wraeclast."
Bring the Verisium to Dannig / Take the Verisium Spikes from Dannig: Dannig crafts Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots

nodes.name: The Runefathers
nodes.summary: Kalguuran runesmiths who gathered after Aldur's death to forge the Triskelion Flame in his honour.

sources.locator: ===The Triskelion Flame===: "After Aldur had passed away, the Runefathers gathered to forge the Triskelion Flame."

nodes.name: Royal Order of Criminal Hanging
nodes.summary: A royal order to hang named criminals that was damaged by seawater on the voyage to Kingsmarch; Johan declined to enforce it because the reply would exceed the Charter's statute of limitations and he would not hang the wrong man.

sources.locator: ==Legal Response (Johan)==: "the recent Royal Order of Criminal Hanging was damaged by seawater"; "the punishment in question will exceed the Charter statute of limitations"

nodes.name: Ban on collecting virtue gems in Kalguur
nodes.summary: After the Azmeri reacted fearfully to virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third officially banned their collection; the gems never returned to Kalguur (Kalguur page, Thaumaturgy section).

chronology.relative: during the reign of Cadigan III (ancient Kalguur)

sources.locator: ===Thaumaturgy===: "after witnessing the Azmeris' fearful reaction towards virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third had officially banned their collection"
